title: Hurricane Matthew—predictions, observations, and an analysis of coastal change
citation: Birchler, J.J., Doran, K.S., Long, J.W., and Stockdon, H.F., 2019, Hurricane Matthew—predictions, observations, and an analysis of coastal change: U.S. Geological Survey Open-File Report OF-2019-1095, map scale 1:19,565,000.
notes: Hurricane Matthew coastal-change report (Florida to North Carolina). Recorded only South Carolina storm-effect sites named in the text (two dune breaches and the Edisto Beach overwash; DFL = distance from landfall). Not recorded: forecast and model values (P-Surge/SLOSH, table 1, contingency tables 6), wave, surge and water-level measurements (hydrologic, not geologic), and state-wide lidar coastal-change statistics (South Carolina: mean dune elevation change -0.5 m, mean shoreline change 6.0 m landward, mean beach volume change +7.2 m3/m, 37 percent of dunes overwashed, page 37), which have no field in the schema. Figures 18-20 (South Carolina coastal-change graphs and maps) have no legible values in the text. References are coastal-process, aerial-photo and storm references; none on South Carolina geology; not recorded.
